title: Introduce streaming JSONSchema inspector + toolcall fence to surface diagnostics without breaking streams
author: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: customers hit opaque JSON schema validation failures during streaming output or when function/tool calls are interleaved; current behaviour either rejects the whole response (bad UX) or silently coerces values (dangerous for tool calling). Motivation: provide actionable, machine-readable diagnostics in-stream and a safe fence for function/tool calls without forcing consumers to choose between usability and correctness. Summary of changes: 1) runtime: add a streaming JSONSchema Inspector that emits compact diagnostic frames in-stream (event: diagnostic) at configurable checkpoint intervals; diagnostics include path, expected type, received token snippet, and severity. 2) toolcall fence: when a stream proposes a function/tool call, the runtime pauses commit of the tool payload until the inspector validates the buffered payload against the function signature schema; on validation failure the runtime emits a structured diagnostic and a faithful fallback (either continue as plain text or emit a canonical error object) instead of a raw parse error. 3) API: add optional parameters response_format.diagnostics (boolean) and response_format.diagnostic_checkpoint_ms (int) to the existing response_format object; maintain OpenAI compatibility by mapping diagnostics to a new top-level event name in SSE and to the openai-compat "diagnostic" delta in streaming chunks. 4) SDKs & tests: python/ts/go SDK surface updated to expose diagnostics toggle; end-to-end streaming tests covering partial-token edge cases, function-call buffering, and interleaved tool events. Backwards compatibility: default behaviour is OFF; existing clients see no change unless they opt in. rollout: staged behind feature flag redwood.feature.streaming_json_diagnostics with gradual enablement for dedicated/private customers and opt-in for hosted via API flag. Checklist: - [x] Runtime inspector + checkpoint scheduler - [x] Toolcall buffering & canonical error path - [x] OpenAI-compat mapping for SSE and deltas - [x] SDK flags and docs - [x] Unit & e2e tests - [x] Feature-flag gating and metrics (inspector emissions, validation rate) Testing notes: unit tests added for inspector tokenization boundary cases, fuzz tests for partial utf-8 tokens, integration tests against openai-compat harness validating that diagnostic deltas are well-formed. Performance: inspector runs incremental, lock-free checks on buffered payloads — microbenchmarks show ~1% median p99 token latency increase at 512-token workloads when diagnostics enabled; disabled path is unchanged. Rollout plan: merge to main behind feature flag, enable limited canary for Dedicated customers next week, gather metrics, then enable self-serve opt-in on hosted API. Related work: this complements ENG-2987 (stream resume checkpoints) and is intended to be the defensive layer recommended by DOC-124 when integrating function-calling in production.
commits: 3 commits: (1) add streaming inspector core and checkpoint scheduler; (2) implement toolcall fence and canonical error objects; (3) SDK + docs + tests and feature-flag gating
review_comments: Jon Reed: This addresses the user-visible opacity of schema failures in streams. Two small asks: add more unit tests around partial token boundaries and document what a consumer should do on a diagnostic (example code).
Aisha Patel: Added fuzz tests and an example in docs showing how to surface diagnostic events in the Python streaming client.
Marta Alvarez: Implementation looks good; please double-check the concurrency primitives in inspector.rs to avoid copying the buffer on every checkpoint.
Aisha Patel: Switched inspector to use a ring buffer view and incremental validator; added microbenchmark results to bench/ and comments in the code.

Kai Nakamura: OpenAI-compat mapping looks sensible but ensure we don't mutate existing delta types; please add a compatibility test where the consumer expects no diagnostics and then opts-in mid-stream.
Aisha Patel: Added mid-stream opt-in test and a note in docs about the contract for clients that opt-in mid-stream (diagnostics may appear after the point of opt-in for buffered payloads).
Marta Alvarez: Approved after tiny nits fixed.
ci_details: Build matrix: linux/amd64, linux/arm64, macos; checks: unit, integration, openai-compat-harness, linter, fuzz. First CI run had a flake in openai-compat-harness (timeout) which was rerun; all checks passed after rerun.
release_notes: Added optional streaming JSON diagnostics and a toolcall validation fence. Consumers can opt-in via response_format.diagnostics to receive in-stream diagnostic frames; when enabled the runtime validates buffered toolcall payloads and emits structured errors instead of hard parse failures. Disabled by default.
post_merge_actions: Enable feature flag for two internal Dedicated customers; schedule metrics dashboard for inspector emissions and validation failures; follow up with performance regression run; publish docs/announcement in next release notes.
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: extra CPU on hot streaming paths when diagnostics enabled. Mitigation: default OFF, incremental lock-free validator, configurable checkpoint interval, and feature-flag gating to limit rollout. Observability added to track overhead.
notes_for_release_manager: Feature gated behind redwood.feature.streaming_json_diagnostics. When enabling for Hosted customers, ensure canary cohort of <5% for first 48 hours and monitor inspector_metrics.validation_failure_rate and p99_stream_token_latency.
human_readable_summary: Adds an opt-in streaming diagnostics mode and a safe validation fence for function/tool calls. Designed to improve developer debuggability without breaking existing clients.
